canonical.title: The staged ladder: what each rung of a Windows→Linux move actually proves

parent.title: Testing the waters: a staged, reversible path from a Windows dev workstation to Linux

siblings.title: WSL2 as rung zero — what it proves, and the exact wall it hits
siblings.summary: WSL2 retires every userland risk in a Linux migration and none of the machine-ownership risks; here is where the line falls in 2026.

siblings.title: Dual-boot Linux next to Windows in 2026 without wrecking the Windows install
siblings.summary: Buy a second NVMe, keep the two OSes ignorant of each other, and pick Linux from the firmware boot menu — the layout with the smallest blast radius on your Windows install.

siblings.title: Dropbox on Linux and shared folders: what actually works in 2026
siblings.summary: The official Linux client now supports btrfs/zfs/xfs, but you cannot share one Dropbox folder between a Windows and a Linux install, and code repos do not belong in Dropbox at all.

siblings.title: Trial hardware and VM paths for evaluating Linux before you commit (2026)
siblings.summary: Live USB first (€10, 15 minutes, proves your actual hardware), then a full install on an external NVMe SSD (€90–150) — everything else is a detour.

siblings.title: Living in both OSes: running Windows and Linux for months without your setup rotting
siblings.summary: One source of truth per asset class, replicated by a tool that knows the OS difference — never a shared partition and never two hand-edited copies.

siblings.title: Exit criteria and the blocker inventory: decide the Linux switch on evidence, not vibes
siblings.summary: A fill-in blocker inventory plus tickable go/no-go criteria and a pre-committed rollback date for a Windows-to-Linux workstation trial.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Comparing WSL versions
sources.claim: WSL2 runs a real Linux kernel with systemd and full syscall compatibility, but uses NAT networking with a changing IP, has no serial-port support, needs usbipd for USB devices, and is slower across the Windows/Linux filesystem boundary.

sources.title: XDA — WSL is great, but run Linux natively instead
sources.claim: WSL2 blocks kernel modules and low-level hardware access, is slow across /mnt/c, and competes with Windows for RAM via vmmem.

sources.title: dspdev.io — Portable Linux on an SSD
sources.claim: Installing Linux to a separate disk makes the rollback trivial — deleting the disk removes the Linux system entirely.

sources.title: WindowsForum — Dual-boot Windows 11 and Linux Mint setup guide
sources.claim: Dual-boot setup requires suspending or decrypting BitLocker before resizing partitions, and disabling Fast Startup because it leaves NTFS volumes hibernated and corruptible when mounted from Linux.

sources.title: BleepingComputer — August updates break Linux boot in dual-boot systems
sources.claim: The August 2024 Windows security update applied an SBAT value that made Linux unbootable on dual-boot systems its detection missed.

sources.title: AnandTech Forums — Should I switch from Windows to Linux? (Feb 2026)
sources.claim: Practitioners in a Feb 2026 thread recommend VM first then spare machine, live USB for hardware enumeration, a spare drive for a real trial of days-to-a-week, separate SSDs per OS, and a used mini PC to avoid dual-boot reboot fatigue.

sources.title: EndeavourOS Forum — Ventoy persistence and kernel updates
sources.claim: Persistent live USB media cannot reliably update the kernel or regenerate initramfs, which blocks installing proprietary graphics drivers.

sources.title: Arch Wiki — PCI passthrough via OVMF
sources.claim: GPU passthrough to a VM requires a spare GPU dedicated to the guest and cooperative IOMMU grouping, so a normal VM cannot represent real desktop/GPU performance.

sources.title: gHacks — How to install Linux on an external SSD
sources.claim: Installing Linux to an external SSD leaves the Windows install intact and is a safe way to run Linux full-time.

sources.title: Microsoft Q&A — WPF and WinForms on macOS and Linux
sources.claim: WPF and WinForms have never been ported to Linux or macOS and Microsoft has no announced plans to do so.

sources.title: Ubuntu Certified hardware
sources.claim: Canonical publishes a searchable list of Ubuntu Certified hardware, usable to check a laptop model before committing.

sources.title: Ubuntu — Try Ubuntu before you install
sources.claim: A live Ubuntu session changes nothing on disk; rebooting without the USB restores the machine exactly.

sources.title: Mykola Aleksandrov — WSL complete practical guide
sources.claim: WSLg lets Linux GUI applications appear alongside native Windows programs in the Start menu and taskbar.

sources.title: NVIDIA — CUDA on WSL user guide
sources.claim: CUDA application development is fully supported under WSL2, but developer tooling such as profilers is still preview-only.

sources.title: Canonical — Desktop certification programme
sources.claim: Canonical's desktop certification runs over 500 OS-compatibility hardware tests per certified machine.

sources.title: Geek Culture — Installing Ubuntu on an external portable SSD, and pitfalls
sources.claim: When installing to an external SSD, the installer can overwrite the internal EFI partition; disabling internal drives in BIOS before install prevents this.

sources.title: WindowsPost — 30 days of Linux vs Windows
sources.claim: A documented 30-day dual-boot Linux trial found days 1-3 smooth, week 1 the friction trough (printer drivers, Bluetooth audio latency, missing apps), and adaptation by week two.

sources.title: Informatec Digital — Linux vs Windows laptop battery consumption
sources.claim: Linux battery life is often worse than Windows out of the box because OEMs ship Windows drivers with power management precisely tuned to the hardware.

sources.title: TLP — Optimize Linux laptop battery life
sources.claim: TLP tunes low-level Linux power management parameters to improve laptop battery life.

sources.title: Linuxiac — Wayland NVIDIA explicit sync support
sources.claim: Explicit sync landed in Wayland and eliminated the long-standing NVIDIA flickering and frame-pacing class of bugs.

sources.title: Microsoft Q&A — BitLocker and dual-boot Ubuntu/Windows 11 NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM
sources.claim: Users report NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM bugchecks on BitLocker-enabled Windows 11 machines dual-booted with Ubuntu.

sources.title: It's FOSS News — Microsoft finally fixes Linux dual-boot bug
sources.claim: Microsoft took roughly nine months to ship a fix for the SBAT update that broke Linux dual-boot.

sources.title: Arch Wiki — System time (RTC localtime vs UTC)
sources.claim: Windows assumes the RTC holds local time while Linux assumes UTC, producing clock skew on dual-boot machines that must be fixed explicitly.

sources.title: How-To Geek — You don't need to dual-boot anymore
sources.claim: The reboot required to switch OSes is the practical failure mode of dual-boot: the friction pushes users to stay in one OS.

sources.title: XDA — 5 pitfalls of dual-booting Windows and Linux
sources.claim: Dual-booting brings unanticipated pitfalls including unpredictable updates and awkward file sharing between the two systems.

sources.title: dev.to — I deleted Windows (and my bootloader)
sources.claim: A dual-booter kept an 800 GB Windows partition and never booted into it once after installing Linux.

sources.title: Xe Iaso — 2026 will be my year of the Linux desktop
sources.claim: In January 2026 Xe Iaso reported not having booted Windows on their tower in over three months, and planned to move to Fedora.

sources.title: Hacker News — 2026 will be my year of the Linux desktop (835 points)
sources.claim: The '2026 will be my year of the Linux desktop' post drew 835 points and 639 comments on Hacker News in January 2026, showing the topic remains actively contested.

sources.title: JetBrains Rider
sources.claim: JetBrains Rider supports .NET, ASP.NET, MAUI, Blazor and Azure development on Linux.

sources.title: About Chromebooks — Windows 11 adoption rate statistics
sources.claim: Windows 10 reached end of support on 14 October 2025 and shed 9.4 points of share between then and June 2026.

sources.title: FOSS Post — Linux market share statistics
sources.claim: Desktop Linux rose from 2.76% in July 2022 to about 4.7% in 2025 and is projected near 6% by late 2026.
